audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart gives Rumble 4/7 stages and Vladimir 0, while Vladimir wins 53.57% over 252 games. whys[5] and whys[6] and the 'late' paragraph already say the lane evens at first item and flips to Vladimir at 2+ items, but win[5]/win[6] and phases[5]/phases[6] still read Rumble.
audit.why: Vladimir's scaling is Crimson Pact (P) converting bonus Health into AP and back, plus Transfusion (Q) falling from 9s to 4.6s. Rumble is cooldown-reliant burst: The Equalizer is 130/105/80s and Flamespitter is 10s down to 6s. Extended fights favour the drain.
audit.corrected: First item = Skill, 2+ items = Vladimir. Rumble keeps levels 2-5.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] credits Rumble's poke to 'Haestream heat'. No such thing exists — Rumble's passive is Junkyard Titan.
audit.why: Fabricated ability name shipped as a power-spike explanation.
audit.corrected: Junkyard Titan heat + Liandry's is the first-item spike; Overheat (100% Heat) is the lockout window that answers it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page names Scrap Shield (W) as the matchup-defining cooldown to bait and track. Scrap Shield is a flat 6-second cooldown — it is never a window. The real punishable states are Overheat (Junkyard Titan locks him out of all spells) and The Equalizer at 130/105/80s.
audit.why: Advice keyed to a 6s cooldown gives the player a window that does not exist and hides the two that do.
audit.corrected: Track Overheat and The Equalizer. Also: The Equalizer creates terrain that cuts your retreat and Vladimir has no dash — hold Flash for the wall, not the damage.

edits.before: Equalizer denies your fight space, keeping Rumble ahead at six.
edits.after: Equalizer denies space, but Hemoplague amplifies and heals you.

edits.before: Rumble's Liandry's plus Haestream heat gives him constant DoT poke — farm from max range and don't walk into Flamespitter.
edits.after: Rumble's Liandry's plus Junkyard Titan heat gives constant DoT poke — farm outside Flamespitter's 600 range and punish his Overheat.

edits.before: His Equalizer (R) carpet burns your whole trade zone; your Hemoplague answers it but you still can't stand in the flames to fight.
edits.after: The Equalizer (R) burns your trade zone on a 130s cooldown at rank 1, and its terrain cuts your retreat — you have no dash, so Flash the wall, not the damage.

edits.before: Riftmaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Scrap Shield's cooldown.
edits.after: Riftmaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, while he is Overheated.

edits.before: - Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining — Bait it, then commit. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Overheat: at 100% Heat Junkyard Titan locks him out of every spell — that is the window, not Scrap Shield's flat 6s. - The Equalizer: 130s at rank 1. - Hemoplague: 120s, kill windows only.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: The Equalizer walls your retreat and you have no dash — Flash the wall.

notes: Scrap Shield (W) is a flat 6s cooldown yet is named the matchup-defining bait-and-punish button in tldr, winCon, enemyWin, ahead, loading, tradeGood, breakdown.mid/spikes/feeding, dosFull[0], report[5], report[9] and report[10]. I corrected the cooldown section, focus and phases[5].why; the remaining strings still carry the same false premise and need a champion-level pass. Also: spikes[3] and whys[6] claim Sanguine Pool 'cleanses' Rumble's burn ticks — the kit only gives 2s untargetability, and whether that removes an existing DoT is not in Riot's text. Left alone, logged unverified.
